chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Everything will perish except for His Face [28:88]'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever comes to Allah with what he has been commanded — namely, obedience to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) — that is the Face (of Allah) which will not perish.' And likewise He (Allah) said: 'Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah [4:80].'

key_terms.طَاعَةِ مُحَمَّدٍ: obedience to Muhammad — the Imam equates this with the 'Face of God' that does not perish
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic (Azza wa Jalla) — honorific epithet for God
key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: His Face — in classical Islamic theology, a divine attribute denoting God's Essence or Presence; here interpreted as obedience to the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What does 'everything will perish except His Face' (Quran 28:88) mean according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides an esoteric interpretation of Quran 28:88 ('everything will perish except His Face'), explaining that 'the Face of Allah that will not perish' refers to obedience to the Prophet Muhammad. The Imam was speaking to Safwan al-Jammal, one of his trusted companions. He reinforces this interpretation with a second Quranic proof (4:80), establishing that true devotion to God is channeled through devotion to His Messenger. This hadith belongs to Al-Kafi's Book on Theological Miscellany, highlighting the Shia understanding that divine proximity is achieved through the Ahlulbayt's guidance.
